description: Use the \" escape sequence to include quotation marks inside a String literal and compare System.out.print with System.out.println.

steps.description: Look at line 3, where \" inside the String literal tells Java to include literal quotation marks around "We've always done it this way!" instead of ending the String early.
Call System.out.println(" -- Grace Hopper") on line 4 right after System.out.print on line 3.

steps.answer: Because line 3 uses System.out.print (without ln), it stays on the same line, so " -- Grace Hopper" prints right after the closing quotation mark on the same line.
steps.question: Does " -- Grace Hopper" on line 4 print on the same line as the quote or on a new line?

steps.description: Step from line 3 to line 4 to see both strings appear on a single output line.

title: Escaping Quotation Marks and Comparing print vs. println
